title: Wave 3 Revision — Places, Reporting & Civic Participation
revisionReason: Reframe Civic Map from a ratings-first destination into one consumer of a shared Makati place registry, while preserving completed asset research, reporting infrastructure, emergency handling, duplicate detection, lifecycle semantics and general participation workflows.
productDoctrine: The verified asset inventory is shared civic-place infrastructure, not a set of objects people are expected to rate.
Civic Map is one interface over the place registry, not the owner of the data.
Public-realm participation should start from a user job: report something, check a place, suggest an improvement or help document Makati.
Generic star-style ratings are retired as a primary interaction; structured observations replace them where useful.
Location and nearby-place matching should reduce the need for users to search for an asset before reporting.
Completed source reconciliation for facilities, parks and transport remains authoritative provenance and is not reopened by this redesign.
Existing case lifecycle semantics remain valid and should be reused.
Metrics and QA are deferred until redesigned workflows stabilize.
preservedCompletedWork: General feedback submission, fallback and public tracking
Civic case duplicate detection and public tracking
explicitlyNotReopened: Transport inventory, ferry, jeepney-route and PNR/NSCR research

GitHub closure and ordinary 'appears resolved' comments do not count as documented resolution.
validation.observationFreshness: Defined from observedAt rather than submittedAt; no universal fresh/stale threshold is set in W3R-10a.
validation.auditCoverage: Defined against each campaign's frozen target set, with separate observed-entity and complete-entity coverage.
validation.repeatContribution: Defined but explicitly not currently measurable reliably; future instrumentation must use a privacy-preserving stable contributor key, never IP address or public alias.
validation.cohortRule: Case metrics use submission cohorts. Later outcomes remain attached to their original cohort; recent cohorts are explicitly right-censored.
validation.implementationBoundary: Definitions only. No analytics, API fields, tracking events, dashboards or public aggregates were added.
validation.focusedValidation: The JSON parses; all five lifecycle states match civic-admin; observation freshness matches observedAt; audit coverage matches frozen target/minimum-observation semantics; repeat contribution is marked not currently ready.

workstreams.title: Define metric publication thresholds
workstreams.maximumScope: Separate internal operational metrics from public metrics and set minimum sample/time thresholds. No dashboards.

caseLifecycle.comparisonRule: Every compared group must independently meet the same publication threshold and equivalent definition; at least three comparable windows are required before calling a pattern a trend.

observationFreshness.aggregateThreshold: At least 10 explicitly eligible entities and at least 5 with observations before publishing an aggregate recent-observation coverage rate.
observationFreshness.entityRule: A single entity's latest observation date/age may be public with sample count; older evidence stays visible but is not labeled stale/poor/noncompliant.

validation.civicAuditCoverage: Public as exact x/y coverage of a frozen target set because the denominator is a campaign census, not a sample. Campaign scope, period, asOf, inventory claim and zero-observation targets remain visible.
validation.repeatContribution: Not currently measurable; after privacy-safe instrumentation it remains internal-only for Wave 3 and never becomes a contributor leaderboard.
validation.suppression: Below-threshold rates are replaced by counts or an insufficient-data label, never 0%.
validation.implementationBoundary: Definitions only. No dashboards, APIs, analytics events, contributor identifiers or UI enforcement were added.
validation.focusedValidation: Threshold JSON parses; all lifecycle rate IDs and companion duration IDs resolve to W3R-10a definitions; sample, maturity, freshness and public/internal rules are explicit.

workstreams.title: Instrument redesigned participation outcomes
workstreams.maximumScope: API/data instrumentation only for fields defined in W3R-10a/10b. No headline aggregates.

civicCaseInstrumentation: Each Civic Report/Proposal record now carries eligibleCivicCase and cohortCreatedAt.
The first reviewed, forwarded, acknowledged, action-reported and community-verified-resolved events are normalized into explicit stage fields.
Per-case elapsed hours to each stage are exposed as raw timing inputs; no medians/rates are calculated.
Routing evidence completeness, acknowledgement authority evidence and lifecycle stage-order anomalies are exposed as diagnostics.
Ordinary community appears-resolved comments remain a separate communityResolutionSignalCount.
observationInstrumentation: Structured-observation GET responses now include latest-observation age, observedAt, sample count, family-specific recent window and hasRecentObservation.
Freshness is calculated from observedAt, never submittedAt.
The no-observation state returns null age/recency rather than a false 0-day reading.
auditInstrumentation: Civic audit responses expose raw numerator/denominator inputs for observed-target and complete-target coverage, plus campaign period, asOf and inventoryClaim.
No percentage is calculated by the instrumentation layer.
A failed audit fetch returns metricInputs=null with dataAvailable=false instead of presenting zero observations as measured zero coverage.
validation.repeatContribution: Deliberately not instrumented. W3R-10a/10b mark it not reliably measurable until a privacy-preserving stable contributor key and retention/deletion policy exist.
validation.implementationBoundary: API/data fields only. No new dashboard cards, public headline rates, medians, rankings or contributor identity tracking were added.
validation.focusedValidation: Shared instrumentation helpers are imported by civic-report, civic-observation and civic-audit; all W3R-10a lifecycle stages, timing inputs, observation freshness and audit coverage inputs are represented without new public aggregate calculations.

workstreams.title: Run human page audit on redesigned participation
workstreams.maximumScope: Participation, Get Involved, Civic Map/place pages and reports only.

validation.keyFinding: Civic Map reports remains partial because its public presentation is still dominated by legacy weekly/monthly volume counts and a three-support proposal threshold rather than the W3R-10 outcome/publication model.
validation.deferred: Dedicated mobile/accessibility browser QA remains W3R-11e; W3R-11a is a manual source-level page audit only.
validation.pageAudit: data/page-audit.json refreshed for all eight scoped routes.

workstreams.title: Add Place Registry integrity audit
workstreams.maximumScope: Guard duplicate IDs, barangays, coordinates, lifecycle states, provenance and broken relationships. No browser testing.

guarded: duplicate registry IDs and lowercase-kebab-case IDs
all registry barangay assignments resolve to one of the 23 current Makati barangays, including slash-separated multi-barangay records
finite WGS84 coordinates, a loose Makati/Metro Manila sanity envelope and exact duplicate-coordinate collisions
identity-source and coordinate-source URL/label pairing plus valid http/https source URLs
verification remains source-derived and legacy mapping status does not silently become lifecycle status
all six allowed lifecycle states remain declared
generated civic-entity-index parity for IDs, names, categories and entity kinds
explicit relationship owner IDs, duplicate relationship tuples, kind/target-type compatibility and referenced target existence
validation.relationshipSources: Current external relationship targets are checked against service, accountability/accountability-supplement, City Monitor and heritage datasets; place targets resolve against the registry itself.
validation.buildIntegration: audit:place-registry is now part of both npm run build and npm run quality immediately after the existing check:place-registry.
validation.focusedValidation: Static source validation reproduced the audit's current snapshot: 88 records, 23 barangays, no duplicate IDs/coordinates, no source-pair problems, full generated-index parity and no broken explicit relationship target.

workstreams.title: Test general participation journeys
workstreams.maximumScope: General submission, duplicate, fallback, tracking and barangay-context E2E only.

journeys: native general submission creates one GitHub issue and returns a public tracking URL/reference
barangay/tool/source metadata survive the native submission body
an exact open duplicate is reused without a second create request
missing native storage returns a pre-filled GitHub fallback while preserving user-entered context
a public issue created through the fallback format can later be recognized by native duplicate detection
Get Involved maps a valid barangay query slug to the canonical barangay name and includes it in the API payload
success, duplicate and fallback UI states expose Track this publicly, Open existing item and Continue on GitHub respectively
Barangay Profile contribution links carry the barangay slug into Get Involved
validation.defectFixed: Fallback GitHub issue bodies previously used plain metadata labels while native duplicate detection expects the canonical bold metadata labels. Fallback and native issue formats now match, allowing fallback-created issues to participate in later duplicate detection.
validation.regression: The existing strong-duplicate regression remains in place; the new journey suite adds native/fallback/tracking/barangay continuity coverage.
validation.buildIntegration: test:participation-journeys now runs from both npm run build and npm run quality after the existing duplicate regression.
validation.focusedValidation: Source validation confirms all journey assertions are represented in the test, API fallback/native metadata now match, Get Involved retains tracking/fallback states, Barangay Profile passes barangay context, and package scripts invoke the suite.
validation.executionBoundary: No GitHub Actions run is available in this repository at this commit, so completion is based on the committed deterministic handler test suite plus focused source validation; no browser/device claim is made.

workstreams.title: Test public-place participation journeys
workstreams.maximumScope: Nearby reporting, place matching, duplicate case, lifecycle, observation and pilot audit E2E only.

journeys: nearby reporting creates a canonical place-backed civic case and server-side canonicalization overrides client-supplied entity name/kind/category metadata
same entity + category + point within 75 metres returns a duplicate candidate instead of a second case
duplicate confirmation writes a civic-comment confirmation to the existing public case
case readback keeps ordinary confirm/appears-resolved signals separate from official lifecycle and advances only through civic-admin evidence
structured observation submission canonicalizes entity metadata, creates/reuses the observation thread and stores the observation as a comment
structured observation readback returns observations ordered by observedAt plus freshness instrumentation
park accessibility audit consumes the same structured observations, excludes out-of-window evidence, applies the frozen 13-target campaign and emits raw observed/complete coverage inputs
defectsFixed: CivicDiscussion expected a legacy destination field while civic-admin stores authority. The discussion now renders authority, with destination retained only as a compatibility fallback.
CivicAuditResults hard-coded /13 in coverage cards and the target heading. It now reads targetCount from live audit output with the frozen campaign length as fallback.
evidenceBoundaries: A community appears-resolved signal does not promote the case to community-verified-resolved.
New native case creation returns unverified/forwarded=false.
Audit output remains count/coverage input based; the journey test rejects an overallScore field.
validation.buildIntegration: test:public-place-journeys now runs from both npm run build and npm run quality after the general participation journey suite.
validation.focusedValidation: Source validation confirms the committed suite covers canonical matching, duplicate confirmation, lifecycle separation, observation submit/readback and pilot-audit aggregation; lifecycle authority and data-driven target-count fixes are present; package scripts invoke the suite.
validation.executionBoundary: No GitHub Actions run is available at this commit, so completion is based on the committed deterministic handler-level journey suite plus focused source validation; dedicated browser/mobile testing remains W3R-11e.

workstreams.title: Run mobile and accessibility pass
workstreams.maximumScope: Redesigned Wave 3 surfaces only. Fix only defects found.

validation.scope: 13 redesigned Wave 3 page/component surfaces plus the shared UI accessibility baseline in src/index.css.
defectsFixed: CivicDiscussion quick actions and text-action controls included 40px or smaller mobile touch targets. Interactive actions now use at least min-h-11 (44px) in the redesigned discussion flow.

CivicDiscussion asynchronous feed/loading/reply-empty failure states were visually present but not consistently announced. Loading states now use role=status and failures use role=alert/dynamic alert semantics.

NearMePlaces changed geolocation state and nearby results without a dedicated live announcement. The component now exposes aria-busy, a polite live status, and an alert for denied/unavailable location.
The Get Involved emergency phone link was a small inline text target. It now has a 44px minimum mobile target while retaining the direct tel:911 action.
existingBaselineConfirmed: global focus-visible outline for links, buttons and form controls
hidden honeypot fields removed from keyboard order and accessibility tree
nearby-report and observation forms expose submitting/status semantics
no hard w-[...], min-w-[...] or whitespace-nowrap mobile locks were found across the 13 scoped Wave 3 surfaces
validation.regressionAudit: scripts/audit-wave3-mobile-accessibility.mjs now guards the responsive-width, touch-target, focus, reduced-motion, async-status and hidden-honeypot markers and is included in both npm run build and npm run quality.
validation.focusedValidation: Current source snapshot passes the audit conditions: 13 scoped surfaces, zero flagged mobile width locks, no min-h-10 controls in CivicDiscussion, Near me live/error semantics present, 44px emergency link target present, and the global reduced-motion/focus/44px control baseline remains intact.
validation.executionBoundary: This was a source-level responsive/accessibility pass. The current environment has no browser/device automation path and the repository has no GitHub Actions run for these commits, so no claim is made about physical-device, screen-reader or automated browser execution.

workstreams.title: Reclassify and close Wave 3
workstreams.maximumScope: Supersede the old capability classification with an evidence-based redesigned Wave 3 classification, record deferrals, and close only what is actually complete.

validation.supersession: data/wave3-participation-classification.json is retained as a historical snapshot but marked superseded by the redesigned classification.
notFullyComplete: Outcome-oriented /civic-map/reports presentation remains partial and is explicitly deferred to a future scoped follow-up.
Repeat-contribution measurement remains deferred until privacy-safe identity/retention design exists.
Public lifecycle rates/medians and aggregate freshness rates remain threshold-gated.
Official participation calendar completeness remains source-dependent.
Physical-device/screen-reader and independently executed CI validation are not claimed.
validation.closureRule: All planned Wave 3 redesign micro-steps are complete, but Wave 3 is not labeled fully complete because the redesigned classification preserves the known partial/deferred capabilities.

streetSegments.consequence: The Segment view can show the three named draft segments, but no Poblacion-wide or Makati-wide street/sidewalk completeness claim is supported.

civicEntityTreatment.place: Destination-like physical sites. Address, access, services-at-location and nearby matching may apply; default browse requires verified status.
civicEntityTreatment.segment: Bounded infrastructure units. Boundary/geometry is primary; representative points are display aids only; provisional named segments can appear as Draft segment.
civicEntityTreatment.route: Network/service records. Route definition and lifecycle are primary; routes are not proximity-matched as nearby places.
civicEntityTreatment.civicCaseIdentity: New civic cases use entityId/entityKind, with placeId/assetId retained only as compatibility fallbacks for older records.

closure.note: Wave 3 redesign execution is closed. Future work must reopen a specifically scoped deferred/partial capability rather than treating the whole wave as unfinished or fully complete.
